entries.content:
The X Parasites, usually called simply the X, are gelatinous, glowing organisms native to planet SR388. In their free state they are translucent blobs that drift through the air. "Parasite" is a loose label; in practice the X are predators. An X enters a living host, feeds and multiplies inside it, and bursts free when the host dies, then uses the victim's DNA to build a perfect mimic that carries the original's appearance, abilities, weaknesses, memories and knowledge. They reproduce asexually by division, so one X becomes many within a short time. Conventional weapons do little to the free-floating form, and a mimicked creature is only slightly tougher than the original; what reliably destroys the X is Metroid tissue, and the Metroids are their only natural predator.

The X were already on SR388 when the Chozo came to the planet. The Thoha, a Chozo tribe of scientists, met the X there and found no way to fight them, so they engineered the Metroids as artificial predators to exterminate the X (recorded in the Chozo Memories; Metroid: Samus Returns). The Metroids drove the X to the edge of extinction but later mutated beyond the Thoha's control. Per the manga, it was the Chozo who first discovered and named the X, after recording one mimicking a Hornoad.

When Samus Aran exterminated the Metroids of SR388 for the Galactic Federation, she unknowingly removed the X's predator. The X recovered and spread through the planet's surviving fauna. On a later escort mission for Biologic Space Laboratories, an X mimicking a Hornoad infected Samus; the Metroid vaccine that saved her made her the only being immune to the X and able to absorb them. X carried to the BSL research station overran it, producing the SA-X and many X-mimicked creatures, until Samus crashed the station into SR388 and destroyed both, with every X on them (Metroid Fusion).

The X are not mindless. Aboard the BSL they adjusted a sector's atmosphere to suit their breeding, went after the Metroids of the Restricted Laboratory, and used a mimicked crewman to sabotage the station's main boiler. Adam observed that the X act for the survival of their species rather than the individual. Samus called them "heartless abominations" and judged that any Federation force sent to capture them would be overwhelmed and absorbed. Years later a living X was recorded on planet ZDR, where Raven Beak had quarantined an outbreak among the Mawkin Chozo inside Elun; the X were released across ZDR and, as far as is known, perished when that planet exploded.
entries.notes: Main overview entry. Metroid-creation backstory draws on Metroid Wiki's X Parasite and Dread pages plus Nintendo's Dread Report Vol. 7 (Chozo Memories cover 'the development of the Metroid species intended to exterminate the X parasite'). The 'Metroids mutated out of control' point rests on the Dread Chozo Archives as summarized by secondary sources.

entries.comment: X Parasite: X biology, mimicry and Core-X
entries.content:
An X infection begins when a gelatinous X touches a living creature. It enters the body and multiplies in the host's nervous system, feeding until the host dies and the swollen X burst out. The X then reads the host's DNA and builds a copy: the mimic looks, moves and fights like the original, inherits its abilities and weaknesses, and holds its memories and knowledge. A living host is not required. The X animated the corpse of Serris, the frozen body of Ridley aboard the BSL station, and later the bodies of Quiet Robe and Kraid on ZDR, and one posed as a golden Chozo Statue. Mimics are only marginally sturdier than the real creature, but all of them carry the X's relentless hostility.

When a mimic is destroyed, the X inside reverts to its gelatinous form and drifts off to seek a new host. In that state beams pass through most of them, Power Bombs do nothing, and only Metroid cells, or a being carrying Metroid DNA, can destroy or consume them. Samus, who carries that DNA, must catch an X in its free form as it escapes its dead host; absorbing it restores her energy and ammunition. The common X are distinguished by color:
- Yellow X, the most common, restore a little energy (ten units). The X that infected Samus on SR388 was yellow.
- Green X restore two Missiles and are often shaken loose from a Core-X struck by beam fire.
- Red X are the rarest. They hide inside the Gadora that guard important hatches and appear before major confrontations. A Red X makes a creature more persistent and durable and changes its color, producing golden Scisers, golden Zebesians and blue Zero. Absorbing one refills four Energy Tanks' worth of energy, ten Power Bombs and fifty Missiles.
- Blue X, larger and smarter, lived only in the frozen Sector 5 (ARC) and Sector 6 (NOC) of the BSL, often hiding under crates. They attack when they can and flee when they cannot, and they are the only X a beam or Power Bomb can stun. Their cold harmed Samus until she recovered the Varia Suit; afterward each yielded thirty units of energy, and once she had absorbed a few the rest fled at the sight of her.

A Core-X is a far larger X, possibly a mass of many, found at the heart of the most powerful hosts; per the original manual it has a thorny membrane. It survives the death of its host, rams anything near it, and sheds Yellow or Green X when shot with beams. Only Missiles crack its spiked shell; absorbing the exposed core returns an ability it had taken along with a flood of energy and ammunition. A Hard Core-X carries a stolen beam weapon that it fires from a single eye, and it can be hurt only by striking that eye while the beam charges; a Missile to the eye makes it fire at once. Core-X appeared again on ZDR, inside mutated creatures such as Escue and Golzuna.
entries.notes: Color-variant numbers (10/30 energy, 2 Missiles, 4 Energy Tanks + 10 Power Bombs + 50 Missiles) are from Metroid Wiki's X Parasite article. The golden Chozo Statue mimic is from Metroid Wiki's Fusion page ('X disguised as a golden statue') and the Nettori page.

entries.content:
The SA-X (a name Adam coined, presumably for Samus Aran-X) is an X Parasite that mimicked Samus Aran herself. When Samus was infected on SR388, the pieces of her Power Suit that had fused with her nervous system were surgically cut away and shipped, still infested, to the Biologic Space Laboratories research station for study. The X inside them had absorbed enough of her to build a complete copy: Samus as she had been at full strength, in the Varia Suit, armed with the Ice Beam, Wave Beam, Super Missiles, Power Bombs and Screw Attack. Adam concluded that the SA-X escaped its capsule in the Quarantine Bay with a Power Bomb, breaching the other specimen capsules and loosing the X on the station (Metroid Fusion).

Its arsenal was everything Samus lacked after the vaccine. The Ice Beam was its deadliest weapon, because her new Metroid DNA made her as vulnerable to cold as a Metroid. It opened a blue hatch with the Ice Beam in Sector 2 (TRO), blasted through a Main Deck wall with Super Missiles, bombed its way through a barrier in Sector 6 (NOC) while Samus hid in a vent as a Morph Ball, and interfered with the heating systems of Sector 3 (PYR). Adam's standing order was blunt: "If you see the SA-X, just run. Don't think about fighting." When it saw Samus it pursued her single-mindedly, somersaulting in Screw Attack when cornered, though it generally lost interest once she left its sight.

Because the X reproduce by asexual division, the SA-X did not stay singular. By the time Samus reached the Restricted Laboratory there were no fewer than ten SA-X aboard. One broke into the laboratory and fired on the Federation's secretly bred Metroids; the Metroids swarmed it, a lockdown began, and the laboratory was jettisoned and exploded with the SA-X inside. Adam then revealed that the Galactic Federation believed the SA-X had "endless potential applications" and meant to capture it, and ordered Samus to leave. She refused.

On her way to redirect the station's orbit, an SA-X cornered her on the Main Deck and forced a fight she could not avoid. Struck hard enough, it swelled into a grotesque, misshapen monster, then collapsed into a blue Core-X and fled before she could absorb it. In the Docking Bay an Omega Metroid attacked Samus, who had no Ice Beam. The SA-X reappeared, charged the Omega Metroid with its Ice Beam, and was struck down into its Core-X form; Samus absorbed it, regaining the Ice Beam and the look of her original Varia Suit, and killed the Omega Metroid. Every remaining SA-X burned with the station when it struck SR388. For Samus the SA-X was her own strength turned against her, the one enemy on the BSL she was ordered never to face.
entries.notes: The claim that the SA-X interfered with Sector 3 (PYR)'s heating systems comes from Metroid Wiki's SA-X page and could not be cross-checked. The 'no fewer than 10' and 'endless potential applications' lines are from the Metroid Recon transcript.

entries.comment: X Parasite: The X outbreak aboard the BSL station
entries.content:
The X outbreak began on SR388 shortly after Samus exterminated the planet's Metroids. The Galactic Federation assigned her to guard a Biologic Space Laboratories (BSL) research team on the surface. She destroyed what appeared to be a Hornoad with a Missile; the creature was an X mimic, and the freed X latched onto her. The X multiplied through her central nervous system, she lost consciousness in her Gunship on the way back, and the ship drifted into an asteroid belt. The security system ejected her in an escape pod, a BSL vessel recovered her, and she was taken to Galactic Federation headquarters. Large portions of her Power Suit had grown into her nervous system and had to be surgically removed, altering her appearance; the X in her nerves could not be cut out. As a last resort she was injected with a vaccine cultured from cells of the Metroid hatchling that had died saving her on Zebes. It destroyed the X, made her immune, and left her with Metroid DNA and a Metroid's vulnerability to cold.

The infested suit pieces and infected SR388 specimens were shipped to the BSL research station orbiting SR388. An explosion in the Quarantine Bay followed, and Samus, in the Fusion Suit and a new Gunship whose computer she nicknamed Adam, was sent to investigate (Metroid Fusion). The explosion had been the SA-X, born from her suit parts, breaking out with a Power Bomb and breaching the other capsules. The X spread through all six sectors, infecting the station's fauna and its remaining crew, and spread further as Samus lifted security locks to move through the station. They acted with purpose: in Sector 1 (SRX) they manipulated the ventilation to create breeding conditions, a mimicked crewman shut down the main boiler's cooling to trigger the self-destruct system, the security robot B.O.X. was taken through its organic neural network, and Nightmare was turned loose in Sector 5 (ARC). Samus reclaimed her abilities one Core-X at a time (see X-mimicked creatures of the BSL).

In the Restricted Laboratory, Samus found the Federation's secret Metroid breeding program. An SA-X attacked the Metroids there, the laboratory was jettisoned and destroyed, and Adam admitted that no fewer than ten SA-X now existed and that the Federation meant to capture them. Samus answered that the moment Federation ships landed the X would overwhelm them and absorb the knowledge and power of their occupants, and resolved to destroy the station even at the cost of her life. The computer, revealing itself as the uploaded mind of Adam Malkovich, proposed altering the station's orbit so that it fell into SR388 and the self-destruct system vaporized every X. Samus survived a final SA-X and an Omega Metroid in the Docking Bay, escaped as the Etecoons and Dachora she had freed moved her Gunship, and watched the BSL station and SR388 destroy each other. The X were believed extinct from that day until a living specimen was recorded on ZDR.
entries.notes: Focuses on the X's role; the station itself, its sectors and the non-X plot belong to the fusion domain and are only referenced. Station-wide timeline deliberately kept loose to avoid duplicating the fusion domain's incident entry.

entries.comment: X Parasite: X-mimicked creatures of the BSL
entries.content:
Every powerful creature Samus faced aboard the Biologic Space Laboratories research station during the X outbreak was an X mimic, and each held a Core-X carrying one of the abilities her damaged suit had lost (Metroid Fusion). Absorbing the core returned the ability.
- Arachnus-X (Main Deck): an X copy of the armadillo-like SR388 native, far more aggressive than the original. Its claws threw waves of energy, its fireballs ran lines of flame along the floor, and it rolled into its shell to ram. Its Core-X returned the Morph Ball.
- Zazabi (Sector 2, TRO): a plant-like hopper with a toothed suction cup for a base, taken by an unusually powerful Core-X. It leapt to swallow Samus and drain her energy; only its inner body could be hurt. Its core returned the Hi-Jump and Spring Ball.
- Serris-X (Sector 4, AQA): the real Serris, a serpent kept in a breeding tank, was found dead; its X copy raced through the tank at blinding speed. Its core returned the Speed Booster.
- B.O.X. (Sector 3, PYR, then Sector 6, NOC): the station's security robot, a hybrid whose organic neural network the X claimed. It first ambushed Samus with fire bombs after destroying the PYR Data Room and fled; in NOC it fought with homing missiles over water its own discharges had electrified. Its core returned the Wave Beam.
- Human Core-X (Sector 3, PYR): an X that had mimicked a crew member, found shutting down the main boiler's cooling unit to detonate the station. It emerged as a Hard Core-X firing the Wide Beam, which Samus took back. From it Adam concluded that "the X can absorb the memories and knowledge of their prey"; the only survivors Samus ever found were the Dachora and Etecoons.
- Mega Core-X (Sector 6, NOC): the X that stole the Varia Suit data from the NOC Data Room, grown huge and ringed by lesser cores. Breaking it returned the Varia Suit and ended the Blue X's threat.
- Nettori (Sector 2, TRO): a plant whose vines spread through the station, blacked out its power and wrapped a Chozo Statue; it fired the Plasma Beam and spat spores. Its Hard Core-X returned the Plasma Beam.
- Nightmare (Sector 5, ARC): the gravity-manipulating Federation weapon from the Bottle Ship, now an X-host. Adam: "It possesses uncommon power and can manipulate gravity." It wrecked ARC and pinned Samus's Missiles to the floor with its gravity field; its core returned the Gravity Suit.
- Yakuza (Main Deck, Reactor Silo): a spider-like creature that seized Samus, slammed her down and spat fireballs during the station-wide blackout. Its core returned the Space Jump.
- Neo-Ridley (Sector 1, SRX): an X that cloned Ridley's frozen body from Sub-Zero Containment; its core returned the Screw Attack (see Neo-Ridley / Ridley-X).
Lesser mimics filled the station too: hostile Hornoad-X on the Main Deck and in SRX, and golden Scisers, golden Zebesians and blue Zero empowered by Red X. Samus had to kill each mimic twice, once as the creature and again as the exposed core before it could escape to a new host.
entries.notes: Neo-Ridley and Nightmare's Bottle Ship origin are owned by the ridley and adam-other-m domains; they are mentioned in one line each with cross-references and are not keyed here. Rewards per Metroid Wiki boss pages; Nettori's Plasma Beam is listed as its reward on the wiki page.

entries.comment: X Parasite: The X on ZDR
entries.content:
After the Biologic Space Laboratories station and SR388 were destroyed, the X were presumed extinct. Then the Galactic Federation received a video transmission of a living X on the remote planet ZDR. Seven E.M.M.I. units sent to investigate fell silent, and Samus, the only being immune to the X, went to ZDR to learn whether the parasites truly survived (Metroid Dread). The footage was bait: Raven Beak, leader of the Mawkin Chozo, had let it reach the Federation so that Samus would come.

The X had reached ZDR through the Mawkin themselves. One of Raven Beak's soldiers carried an X, and the infection swept the tribe until every Chozo on the planet except Raven Beak and the Thoha survivor Quiet Robe was infected. Raven Beak sealed the infected inside Elun, a fortress-like quarantine in a rocky cavern below the surface, and replaced his lost warriors with Robot Chozo Soldiers. The outbreak, together with Samus's extermination of the Metroids, wrecked his plan to bring Metroids to ZDR and turned him toward cloning a Metroid army from her DNA.

Samus's path led her into Elun, where the sealed halls were thick with X and mutated Mawkin. A Chozo Soldier animated by the X challenged her with a spear; as the fight went on its head warped into a beaked, Raven Beak-like shape and it sprayed black ooze, until she blasted it from inside its own mouth and absorbed the X. As she left, Raven Beak opened the door behind her, deliberately loosing the X across ZDR to push her Metroid powers to awaken. Adam suspected his hand immediately.

The X spread planet-wide. Creatures they possessed grew stronger and, when killed, left Yellow, Green and Red X for Samus to absorb. An X took the corpse of Quiet Robe and reactivated the E.M.M.I. he had shut down. Experiment No. Z-57, a specimen from the Dairon laboratory, was taken over and cut off the thermal energy flowing from Cataris, freezing ZDR until Samus destroyed it. A Quetzoa on Ferenia became Escue and a Muzby on Ghavoran became Golzuna, and their Core-X yielded Storm Missiles and Cross Bombs. X-mimicked Chozo Soldiers in silver, red and gold Elite forms met her in several regions, each shifting into a monstrous shape partway through combat.

Aboard Itorash, Samus drained Raven Beak with her awakened Metroid powers. As he rose to fight again, a purple X, one that had earlier claimed Kraid's body in Cataris, infected him and produced Raven Beak X, a hybrid of Raven Beak and Kraid, which Samus obliterated with the Hyper Beam of her Metroid Suit. Fully Metroid, she could not board her Gunship without draining it. The X wearing Quiet Robe's form appeared, bowed to her, reverted to its gelatinous state and let itself be absorbed, stabilizing her, and she lifted off as ZDR exploded. With the planet went the last known X in the universe.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki has no pages for Elun, Chozo Soldier, Experiment Z-57, Raven Beak X or the Chozo Archives; those details rest on Wikipedia's plot, Metroid Wiki's ZDR/Raven Beak/Quiet Robe pages, and search snippets from Wikitroid, TV Tropes and guide sites. Z-57 being X-possessed and the Kraid-X identity of the X that infected Raven Beak are from those secondary sources. Escue, Golzuna, Z-57 and Kraid are only mentioned in passing (owned by the dread domain).

entries.comment: X Parasite: Samus and the X
entries.content:
Samus Aran is the only being in the universe known to be immune to the X Parasites, and the only one who can consume them. The immunity was an accident of survival. Infected by an X mimicking a Hornoad on SR388, she was dying as the X multiplied through her central nervous system; the parts of her Power Suit fused to her nerves were cut away, and the Galactic Federation's last option was an experimental vaccine cultured from cells of the Metroid hatchling. It killed every X in her body. In her own words, she owes the hatchling her life twice over (Metroid Fusion).

The vaccine rewrote her. Metroid DNA now runs through her body, the X cannot take hold in her, and she can absorb a free-floating X by touch, drawing it in as nourishment: Yellow X mend her, Green X replenish her Missiles, Red X restore nearly everything, and a Core-X returns an ability it stole along with a surge of energy and ammunition. She must catch the X in its gelatinous form as it flees a dead host; a mimic has to be killed first. The price was a Metroid's weakness to cold, which made the Ice Beam of the SA-X lethal to her until she regained the Varia Suit, and the Metroid nature that later awoke fully on ZDR (see Samus Aran – Metroid DNA, Chozo DNA and what she has become; Fusion Suit). Per the original manual, the X react violently to Metroid tissue and attack her viciously and relentlessly whenever she is within reach.

Her view of the X is unsentimental. She called them "heartless abominations" and dismissed the Federation's talk of their potential. When ordered off the BSL station so the Federation could capture the SA-X, she reasoned that as soon as Federation ships landed the X would overwhelm them and absorb the knowledge and power of their occupants; she chose to destroy the station, and SR388 with it, rather than obey. She treats the X as an intelligent enemy that fights for its species: she has watched them adjust a sector's air for breeding, hunt the Metroids of the Restricted Laboratory, and send her own likeness to kill her.

The SA-X, a copy of herself at full strength, is the X she knows best; Adam's order was to run from it, and she did until she could not. On ZDR, immune and forewarned, she went to confirm whether the X still lived, absorbed the X of an infected Chozo Soldier in Elun, destroyed the X-infected Raven Beak, and at the end accepted the sacrifice of the X wearing Quiet Robe's form, which gave itself up to her to steady her Metroid body (Metroid Dread). She chose to destroy a planet rather than let the X leave it.
entries.notes: Samus's quotes ('heartless abominations', 'owe the Metroid hatchling my life twice over', the Federation-ships line) are from the Metroid Recon Fusion transcript. Her Metroid DNA and physiology are owned by samus-bio and only cross-referenced.

result.research_notes: Coverage gaps and caveats: (1) Metroid Wiki has no articles for Elun, Chozo Soldier (Dread), Experiment No. Z-57, Chozo Archives, Raven Beak X, Metroid Suit, Itorash, Mawkin, Thoha, Cataris, Escue or Golzuna (all 404); its own Metroid Dread page stops its story at the X release. Dread's X material therefore rests on Wikipedia's plot summary, Metroid Wiki's ZDR / Raven Beak / Quiet Robe pages, an Inverse ending article, an omegametroid Elun walkthrough, and search snippets quoting Wikitroid, TV Tropes and game8 (Wikitroid itself and its breezewiki mirror were blocked). (2) Experiment No. Z-57 being X-possessed (a Dairon specimen that blocked Cataris's thermal flow) comes from TV Tropes and guide snippets only; its reward conflicts across guides, so none is stated. (3) The identity of the X that infected Raven Beak as the one that took Kraid's body is stated by Wikipedia and Wikitroid snippets ('purple X', 'hybrid of Kraid and Raven Beak'); Metroid Wiki's Kraid and Raven Beak pages do not cover it. The Hyper Beam finish is from fan-wiki snippets. (4) The silver / red / gold Elite Chozo Soldier variants and their mid-fight X transformation are from Wikitroid and game8 snippets. (5) The SA-X tampering with Sector 3 (PYR) heating is asserted only by Metroid Wiki's SA-X page. (6) Metroid Wiki's X Parasite page says the manga shows the Chozo discovering and naming the X and recording a Hornoad mimic; used with 'per the manga'. The same page's claim that the manga shows Metroids destroying an SA-X was omitted as it could not be reconciled with the 2002-2004 manga's timeframe. (7) No Dread transcript could be fetched (shinesparkers 404), so Dread lines are paraphrased from secondary summaries; Samus's 'only being in the universe with immunity' is from Metroid Wiki's Dread page. (8) Red X 'four Energy Tanks' figure is Metroid Wiki's wording. (9) The Chozo Archives' exact text was not obtainable; their content is summarized from Nintendo's Dread Report Vol. 7 and secondary summaries of the Thoha story.
